title: Constituent-nonexceptional versus Fourier-nonexceptional
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$.

1. If $\mathcal M$ is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional], then its middle extension
$j_*\mathcal M$ is Fourier-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-fd-nonexceptional].
2. If moreover the geometric fundamental representation of
$\mathcal M$ is irreducible, the converse holds: the two notions then
coincide.

proof.text: Put $U=U_0\otimes_{k_0}k$. Use the explicit condition on $U$ in the statement of [def-fd-nonexceptional]: $j_*\mathcal M$ is Fourier-nonexceptional if and only if $\mathcal M|_U$ is not geometrically constant and there is no $a\in k$ for which $\mathcal M|_U$ is geometrically irreducible and has $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ as a geometric constituent. Thus its negation is precisely the disjunction of these two exceptional alternatives. This uses the stated geometric-sheaf condition, with ordinary middle extension and the same lisse adic coefficients as in that definition.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (translation of Fourier-nonexceptionality to U)

proof.text: Assume constituent-nonexceptionality and suppose that $j_*\mathcal M$ is Fourier-exceptional. If $\mathcal M|_U$ is geometrically constant, [rem-dl-a1-conventions] says it is a finite direct sum $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^{\oplus r}$. Here $U$ is connected and nonempty (it is a dense open of $\mathbf A^1_k$), and $r>0$ since $\mathcal M$ is nonzero. The flag by the first $i$ summands, $0\leq i\leq r$, has trivial rank-one successive quotients, so the trivial rank-one sheaf is a Jordan–Hölder constituent. By [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] this is $\mathcal L_{\psi(0\cdot x)}|_U$, which is excluded. In the other exceptional alternative of Step 1, the Artin–Schreier constituent is already explicitly present, again contradicting [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Both alternatives are impossible, proving the first implication.

Assume now that the geometric fundamental representation of $\mathcal M$ is irreducible and that $j_*\mathcal M$ is Fourier-nonexceptional. If constituent-nonexceptionality failed, [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] would give some $a\in k$ with $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ as a geometric constituent. Together with the assumed geometric irreducibility this is exactly the second exceptional alternative excluded by [def-fd-nonexceptional], a contradiction. In the blueprint’s equivalent isomorphism formulation, an irreducible representation has itself as its sole Jordan–Hölder constituent. This proves the converse under the additional hypothesis, and Step 2 gives the equivalence.
